spo2.label: Blood oxygen saturation (SpO2)
assumed: whole measure: typical healthy range 95-100 %, no trend; replace with a cited source

hrv_rmssd.label: Heart-rate variability (RMSSD)
assumed: whole measure: typical adult range, no trend; replace with a cited source

heart_rate.label: Heart rate (spacesuit, during a spacewalk)
assumed: whole measure: resting heart rate that day plus 0.2 to 0.5 of the way to maximum, changing with each task (instruments.eva_heart_rate); replace with a cited source

watch_hr.label: Heart rate (watch, every 15 minutes)
assumed: whole measure: the wearable's 24-hour trace (resting level, daily rhythm, sleep dip, exercise and spacewalks; instruments.day_heart_rate) averaged over 15 minutes; replace with a cited source

sleep_hours.label: Sleep (watch, hours per night)
sleep_hours.source: Barger et al. 2014, Lancet Neurology: 6.09 h a night on the ISS (85 astronauts)
assumed: 6.9 h before and after flight
6.09 h in flight (Barger 2014)
about 0.6 h of night-to-night variation
a fatigue spell takes about 1.6 h

sleep_quality.label: Sleep quality (self-rated, 1 to 7)
sleep_quality.source: scale from OCHMO-STD-100.1A [6039] (1 very poor to 7 excellent)
assumed: the score follows the hours slept: 4.8 at 6.1 h, about +0.9 per extra hour, 1.5 lower in a fatigue spell

oct_trt.label: Retinal thickness around the optic disc (OCT)
oct_trt.source: consensus 2026 (Eye): +20 um earliest indication, +55 um clinically concerning; 66-69 % pass +20 um
assumed: pre-flight 430 ± 30 um
+30 ± 24 um on flight day 150, so the published shares hold

oct_mrw.label: Optic nerve rim width (OCT, BMO-MRW)
oct_mrw.source: Macias 2020 (JAMA Ophthalmol): +35.7 um on flight day 150, 11 astronauts
assumed: pre-flight 400 ± 50 um
follows retinal thickness, 1.19 times its change

oct_choroid.label: Choroid thickness (OCT)
assumed: pre-flight 170 ± 40 um
spread between people ± 15 um

frisen_grade.label: Optic disc edema (Frisén grade)
frisen_grade.source: Frisén scale 0-5; ~15 % of long-duration crew reach grade 1 (Lee 2020)
assumed: grade 1 from +55 um retinal thickness, 2 from +90 um, 3 from +130 um

choroidal_folds.label: Chorioretinal folds
assumed: in the people with the most choroid swelling

globe_flattening.label: Flattening of the back of the eye
assumed: seen on ultrasound in flight; MRI confirms it on the ground

refraction_se.label: Refraction (spherical equivalent)
refraction_se.source: consensus 2026: a shift over +0.50 D in 20 %; Mader 2011: +0.50 to +1.75 D
assumed: pre-flight -0.5 ± 1.5 D
shift +0.2 ± 0.36 D, partly kept after landing

near_va.label: Near vision without glasses (logMAR)
near_va.source: Mader 2011: about 60 % report worse near vision on long missions
assumed: about one chart line (0.1 logMAR) per +0.5 D of shift

iop.label: Eye pressure (tonometry)
iop.source: no public flight values; bed rest 12.9 to 13.9 mmHg (NTRS 2014)
assumed: pre-flight 14 ± 2.5 mmHg
+1 mmHg in flight

onsd.label: Optic nerve sheath diameter (ultrasound)
onsd.source: ONSD review 2022: 5.98 mm pre-flight, +0.91 mm in flight against post-flight
assumed: +0.9 ± 0.35 mm in flight, within about 10 days
back within a week after landing

axial_length.label: Length of the eye
axial_length.source: Macias 2020: -0.08 mm after flight, -0.05 mm a year later
assumed: pre-flight 24.0 ± 0.9 mm

ijv_csa.label: Area of the internal jugular vein
ijv_csa.noise_source: ultrasound area, about ±8 % (assumed; the study accepted 10 % between sonographers)
ijv_csa.source: Marshall-Goebel 2019 (JAMA Netw Open), left vein: 80.7 mm2 supine pre-flight, 70.3 on flight day ~50, 60.0 on day ~150; Arbeille 2015: back to baseline 4 days after landing
assumed: pre-flight read supine: left 80 ± 22, right 100 ± 28 mm2
in flight 0.72 + 0.27·exp(-day/80) of it, ± 12 % between people

ijv_flow_grade.label: Blood flow in the vein (grade 1-4)
ijv_flow_grade.source: Marshall-Goebel 2019: grade 3 in 5 of 11 and grade 4 in 1 on flight day 50; grade 3 in 2 of 10 on day 150, one more grade 4
assumed: left: P(grade >= 3) 55 % on day 50, 30 % on day 150; P(grade 4) 10 %
right: 3 % and 1 %
exam-to-exam correlation 0.75

ijv_echogenicity.label: Slow-blood echoes in the vein (0-2)
ijv_echogenicity.source: Pavela 2022 (Vasc Med): mild-moderate in the left vein of 6 of 11, never more than mild in the right
assumed: follows the stagnant flow score

ijv_compressible.label: The vein collapses when pressed
ijv_compressible.source: OCHMO-STD-100.1A [6041] compression manoeuvre; a vein that does not collapse suggests a clot
assumed: 1 in 14 crew members get a left thrombus between flight days 35 and 70
the clot lies flat 30 days after landing

ijv_peak_velocity.label: Peak blood speed toward the heart
ijv_peak_velocity.source: Pavela 2022: lower in flight, lowest in the left vein (no values published)
assumed: pre-flight supine left 32 ± 9, right 40 ± 10 cm/s
in flight × 0.55 left, × 0.75 right; negative when retrograde
